name: auth-auth0-jwt
title: Auth — Auth0 access tokens (bring your own auth)
description: Use Auth0 as the identity provider and let Auth0 own the session: verify each request's Auth0 access token against your tenant's JWKS and API audience, and feed the user, permissions, scopes and organization into ctx.auth / RLS via a resolveIdentity adapter. For Auth0 as a login button on a Lunora-owned better-auth session, use auth-auth0 instead.
docs: Pass `auth0Identity(env)` as `resolveIdentity` in your Worker entry (`createWorker({ resolveIdentity: auth0Identity(env), … })`, or `.extend((env) => ({ resolveIdentity: auth0Identity(env) }))` on the generated app builder). On the client, create the LunoraClient with `authTokenOnUpgrade: true` and call `setAuthTokenProvider(client, fetchToken, { subject: user.sub })` from `@lunora/client`, where `fetchToken` returns `getAccessTokenSilently()` and maps a `login_required` error to `null`. Guide: https://lunora.sh/docs/concepts/external-auth

envVars.name: AUTH0_DOMAIN
envVars.description: Your Auth0 domain (e.g. acme.us.auth0.com) or custom domain. Not a secret.

envVars.name: AUTH0_AUDIENCE
envVars.description: Your API's identifier from Dashboard → Applications → APIs; access tokens must name it in aud. Not a secret.
